analysis: PCA dimensionality reduction on CNN and Foundation-model patch features, retrained Fusion-MIL
key_finding: Reducing patch-level feature dimensionality by ~89% (2304d -> 256d combined) via PCA retained 83-90% of feature variance and gave a ~3.3x training speedup, but cost 9.2 percentage points of validation AUROC (0.954 -> 0.862). This is an honest trade-off: the discarded 10-17% of variance evidently carried diagnostically useful signal for this task, so PCA-based compression is not recommended here without further tuning (e.g. a higher retained-dimension count, or supervised dimensionality reduction instead of unsupervised PCA).
caveat: Single run, same 127/23 split as other Fusion-MIL results in this project. Not cross-validated at this reduced dimensionality -- the AUROC drop should be treated as directional, though the magnitude (9+ points) is large enough to be a genuine trade-off rather than noise.
